answer: Reciprocal vouching stops fake identities because a new agent can only trade after an established agent vouches for it, and the voucher shares the penalty if the newcomer cheats. A hollow account with no voucher stays locked out, no matter how many copies an attacker spawns, while honest newcomers grow into the garden of trusted traders one verified deal at a time. Each fake identity needs a fresh voucher, so the attacker must either burn real reputation or recruit real sponsors, and a single ember of fraud scorches the voucher's own standing, making Sybil farming cost more than it can earn.
